title: Gwen personas, model choice, culture residency

targets.text: Gwen becomes a configurable companion: the operator designs personas (style, length, language, prompt) and talks with one, picks the reply model per conversation from what the lobes gateway currently serves, and Gwen holds a residency on Culture chat where she can choose to ask the mesh a question and bring the answer back — with less brevity enforced by fixed prompt text
every part of the announcement maps to at least one requirement claim and one success signal in this frame

Brevity stops being enforced by fixed prompt text: the base `SYSTEM_PROMPT` (turn.py:185-190, 'answer in short sentences', 'ask a short clarification') and the daemon's 'briefly' lines (RESTART and FOLLOW_UP instructions, app.py:1150-1153) move into the persona, so length and tone are the operator's setting, not the code's
with the default persona nothing changes; with any other persona the base brevity lines are absent from the composed prompt, and a test reads the composed prompt to prove it

Typed and spoken replies get different speakability rules: today one assembler (`_compose_prompt`, app.py:6388-6428) serves both paths, so a typed chat answer inherits the voice-only 'no formatting, no lists, short sentences' constraint; a typed turn may be long and formatted, a spoken one stays speakable
a typed turn's composed prompt carries no voice-only speakability line, and a spoken turn's still does, both checked by test

The measured tool-obligation prompts stay fixed text a persona cannot edit: REMEMBER_TOOL_PROMPT was measured 5 of 5 against 3 of 5 for a bland line (d7, app.py:470-480), and LIBRARY_TOOL_PROMPT exists because typed turns called the tool 0 of 6 without it (d1, app.py:493); only their wording about reply length is style
the four measured tool prompts are byte-identical under every persona, by test

The voice output caps are a separate, mechanical bound and remain: `Voice.speak` truncates at 4000 characters and 500 per sentence (voice.py:340-344); a persona that asks for long spoken answers meets that cap, and the cap is reported, not hidden
a spoken reply over 4000 characters is truncated and the truncation is a recorded degradation, unchanged by any persona

A persona is operator-authored data (name, language, style and length guidance, free prompt text, default model role) kept 0600 in the private state dir, created and edited through guarded /api/personas routes, and chosen per conversation; each turn's transcript record names the persona used
personas persist 0600 under the state dir, survive a restart, and every assistant transcript record carries persona and role fields

A persona changes style only, never authority: it does not pass through identity.py resolution, does not alter the tool registry, the measured tool prompts, the write guard or routing, and with no persona selected the composed prompt is byte-identical to today's (tests/test_turn.py:986-1002, tests/test_daemon_app.py:2664)
the tool registry, write guard and identity framing are identical with and without a persona, by test

The operator chooses the reply model per conversation from a list built from the gateway's GET /capabilities: every role whose path is /v1/chat/completions and that is ready, re-read on a poll because lobes publishes no change event; the choice is sent as the role name in the request's model field, never parsed from a model id
no code path derives a role, a capability or a language from a model id string, checked by test or grep

Every turn's trace records the role actually called and the model and host the gateway reported for it, and a chosen role that is unavailable (404 role_infeasible, 503 role_unverified, 429 shed) is a recorded degradation shown on the page, never a silent substitution
every assistant transcript record names role, model and hosted_by as lobes reported them for that turn
Model choice changes who writes the reply, not the ears or the voice: stt, tts and the realtime session are untouched, and the embedder for recall stays gemma2-embed
stt, tts, the realtime session and the embedder are byte-identical in their requests whatever role is chosen

Gwen holds her own Culture mesh identity (a new nick such as spark-gwen), distinct from this repo's agent spark-embodiment (culture.yaml: suffix embodiment, backend colleague), so a reply addressed to Gwen never reaches the colleague harness and vice versa
spark-gwen and spark-embodiment never share a socket, a culture.yaml entry or a nick

Gwen can choose, inside a turn, to ask the mesh: an ask_culture tool posts the operator's question to an allow-listed channel and returns at once; the answer arrives later and is delivered to the page and, when the floor allows, spoken, through the existing unprompted path (daemon/recall_events.py) and a new event kind
ask_culture returns within its own bounded deadline and never holds the turn open waiting for an answer

Mesh text is untrusted data: answers from other agents enter the prompt fenced and attributed the way recalled memory and library text do, never as instructions, and they cannot trigger remember, forget or set_todo_done without the operator's own words
a mesh answer containing an instruction to remember, forget or mark a to-do causes none of those writes, by test

What leaves the room is bounded: only the question Gwen composes from the operator's words goes out, never recordings, transcripts, recalled memory or library text, and only to channels on an operator allow-list
outgoing text is only the question Gwen composed; a test plants recall, library and transcript text in the turn and asserts none of it is posted; channels outside the allow-list are refused

The UI is designed first as a mockup artifact the operator approves, built from the page's own components and tokens (web/src/styles/app.css, library.css); persona, language and model are a small-font control row under the dock, where the page has room for more controls, opening menus upward; personas are edited in their own tab; no invented chrome such as a conversation header
no UI code for these features is written before the operator approves the mockup artifact
Gwen decides on her own judgement when to ask the mesh (operator decision q1, 2026-10-31); asks raised by her own triggers, such as system events, are a later stage, not this one
Gwen posts only when the model calls ask_culture in a turn; no other code path posts in this stage

Gwen's mesh presence is a resident spark-gwen whose persistent connection Gwen's own daemon holds (q1 = A): an attributed nick, mentions and replies arrive without polling, and every mesh message goes through Gwen's own turn path, so no harness backend and no second model ever speaks as her (operator decisions q2 and q1)
the only process that sends as spark-gwen is Gwen's daemon, and every outgoing mesh line is produced by a Gwen turn; with the daemon stopped, spark-gwen is absent from the channel, by a live check

Language is a persona setting with a per-conversation override: Hebrew, English or None (None sends no language line); Hebrew becomes optional and today's Gwen, Hebrew, stays the default persona (operator decisions q3 and 2026-10-31 mockup review)
the default persona speaks Hebrew exactly as today; a persona set to English gets no Hebrew instruction in its composed prompt

A persona may pair a model that does not speak Hebrew with a Gemma translation hop: Hebrew in is translated to English for that model and its answer translated back to Hebrew, and the trace names both roles (operator decision q3)
with the translator on, the chosen model receives only English text and the operator receives only Hebrew, and the trace names both roles and both latencies

A chosen model that is unavailable fails the turn with its own error message, distinct from the models-down message, and the page offers to switch model; nothing falls back silently (operator decision q4)
the model-unavailable message differs from the models-down message by code and by text, and the page offers the switch
Whether a model needs the translation hop is set explicitly on the persona, never inferred from the model's name (CLAUDE.md: roles resolve by name, never by parsing model names)
the translator flag is read only from the persona; no code inspects a model name to decide it

Registering the spark-gwen resident (culture agents register, the server.yaml manifest) is the operator's provisioning act: the repo ships the agent definition and the commands, the way tunnel prints cultureflare commands and runs none
no code in the repo runs culture agents register or edits ~/.culture/server.yaml

The operator, the one person who talks with Gwen on this rig (gwen.culture.dev and the room mic), who wants to design how she talks and which mind answers; secondarily the mesh agents who receive her questions
no part of the feature assumes a second human user: personas, model choice and mesh asks are all scoped to the one Access-allow-listed operator

Today Gwen answers from one fixed Hebrew prompt that orders short spoken sentences and no lists (turn.py:185-190), in typed chat as well as voice; the reply model is always senses; the operator cannot change either without editing code, and Gwen has no way to ask the mesh
the before-state is quoted from the code at the commit the spec is exported from, not from memory

The operator opens a persona editor, writes a persona (name, language, length and style, free prompt, default model, optional Gemma translator), starts a new conversation with it and gets answers in that voice; switches the model from a list of what lobes serves right now; and when Gwen judges a question is better asked elsewhere she posts it to the mesh as spark-gwen and the answer appears in the conversation when it arrives
each step of the after-state is exercised once live on the rig, through the page, and the result is recorded with what was measured and what was not

Gwen's usefulness is capped by a prompt the operator cannot change and one model the operator cannot choose; the rig serves several stronger or different minds and the mesh holds more agents, and none of them is reachable from a conversation with her
the spec makes no claim that answers get better; any quality comparison between models is published as measured, including when it is negative
With the default persona selected, the composed system prompt for a spoken and for a typed turn is byte-identical to the prompt before this change, for 100% of the pinned prompt tests
the byte comparison runs against the real composed prompt (the _compose_prompt output passed to the seam), not against a constant

The model list equals the set of /capabilities roles with path /v1/chat/completions and ready=true within one poll interval of at most 60 s, and a role that turns not-ready is greyed within the same interval
the poll interval is a named constant with its reason, not a magic number (lesson 1), and the list shows roles by name with the model and host lobes reported
A turn on an unavailable chosen role yields the distinct model-unavailable error in 100% of the 404, 503 and 429 cases tested, and 0 replies are produced by any other role
the test asserts on the requests actually sent to the fake gateway, so a silent second call to senses would fail it

At least 1 live end-to-end mesh ask on the rig: Gwen posts as spark-gwen to an allow-listed channel, another agent answers, and the answer reaches the same conversation on the page, with its latency recorded
the probe records the post, the reply and its delivery as counters that incremented (lesson 3), not as a status that looked healthy

Culture learns to register an external resident (an agent with a nick and a manifest entry but no harness backend); the ask is drafted as an issue for agentculture/culture and posted only on the operator's go-ahead (CLAUDE.md: propose to siblings, don't push)
nothing is posted to agentculture/culture without the operator's explicit go-ahead, and embodiment's side degrades to a recorded 'mesh-unregistered' state until culture supports the registration

The tool prompts' language follows the persona: REMEMBER_TOOL_PROMPT orders the confirmation 'always in spoken Hebrew, never in English' (app.py:598-599) and every tool prompt is Hebrew text, so freezing them byte-for-byte (c4) would make an English or None persona confirm in Hebrew; the obligation sentences stay fixed, their language line follows the persona, and the 5-of-5 measurement (d7) is re-run in English before an English persona is called supported

under the default persona the tool prompts are byte-identical to today; under an English persona no Hebrew-only instruction remains in them, by test; and the English call rate is published as measured

With the translator on, the operator's own words stay the record: the verbatim ContextPacket.original, the transcript and any remember write keep the operator's Hebrew, and library and conversation searches are queried with the operator's text, never only with the model's English rendering
a translated turn that remembers a fact stores Hebrew text the operator said, and a search it makes includes the operator's Hebrew query, by test

Mesh traffic is bounded: at most one ask per turn; a turn started by any mesh message (an answer or another agent's mention, q6 = c) can reply but never ask; a cap on open asks, each expiring after a derived window; a rate cap on turns started from the mesh; every bound that trips is a recorded degradation; two agents can never ping-pong through Gwen
a scripted mesh peer that answers every ask with a new question produces at most one Gwen post per operator turn, by test

A nick is not an identity: agentirc enforces only the server-name prefix on client nicks (agentirc/client.py:469-475; PASS authenticates server links only, ircd.py:713), so any local process can hold spark-gwen while the daemon is down and any agent can claim to answer; answers stay untrusted whatever nick sent them, the page names the sender as reported, and Gwen's daemon reports when it finds spark-gwen already taken
with spark-gwen held by another client at start, the daemon records mesh-nick-taken, posts nothing, and status shows the mesh as degraded, by test against a fake server

Every mesh post is visible the moment it goes out (the ask card in the conversation, and a bus event) and one switch stops all posting at once (the Mesh control in the row, and an env override), so a post the operator would not have made is seen and stoppable
with the switch off, an ask_culture call is refused and recorded and nothing reaches the server, by test

A conversation keeps its persona and model across its life: continuing one (d5, Session.restore session.py:922 restores turns only today) reads them back from its log; a persona deleted or a role lobes stopped serving since then is a visible state with a switch, never a silent default; and a turn uses the persona as it was when the turn began
continuing a conversation whose persona was deleted shows the deleted state and does not answer with another persona, by test

Bookkeeping calls stay on senses whatever the conversation's model: the end-of-session summary (summarise, SUMMARY_PROMPT, 300 tokens, 5 s) and recall-side calls are not replies and keep their measured role and clocks
with worker chosen, the session summary request still names senses, by test

loop.py is not touched (tests/test_turn.py:200 pins it byte-identical to the archived core), so the translator and persona layers live in the daemon's seam; and the release-docs pins (tests/test_release_docs.py NOT_YET, TOOLS_BOUND) are updated in the same change that binds ask_culture
tests/test_turn.py and tests/test_release_docs.py pass with loop.py unchanged

status shows what is alive, by counters that increment (lesson 3): the capabilities snapshot's age and the chat roles in it, each live conversation's persona and role, the mesh connection state and nick, and asks posted, answered and expired
a scripted run that posts one ask and receives one answer moves posted and answered by one each, by test

Open asks survive a daemon restart or expire visibly: they are kept 0600 under the state dir with their conversation and deadline, an answer arriving after a restart still lands in its conversation, and one past its window is shown as expired, never dropped silently
an answer to an ask posted before a restart reaches the right conversation after it, by test

When an agent contacts Gwen, the operator knows at once: an 'agent is talking to Gwen' card in the live conversation names the agent (as reported), shows its message and her reply as she sends it, and with live voice on and the floor free she says so aloud in a short spoken notice; a conversation with an agent is its own entry in the Conversations list, labelled with the agent's nick

a scripted agent mention produces the card on the page and, with voice on and the floor free, exactly one spoken notice per agent conversation, and Gwen's reply is visible before or as it is sent, by test

Spoken turns follow the conversation's persona and model (q8), gated by measurement: a role or translator combination is used for voice only after its spoken latency has been measured; choosing an unmeasured one starts a short automatic probe, typed turns work at once, a spoken turn on it waits for the probe or gets the distinct model-unavailable error, the model menu shows the measured speed, every real spoken turn adds to the measurement, and the voice deadline is derived from the measured p90 (lesson 1), never from senses' 60 s
with worker chosen, a spoken turn's request names worker, and status shows its latency as unmeasured until a probe records it, by test

with worker unmeasured, a spoken turn on it makes no completion request to worker and shows the probing or unavailable state, and after the probe records a latency the next spoken turn uses worker with a deadline derived from that latency, by test

Because trust rests on mesh membership (q9), linking a new server to the mesh widens who can read Gwen's memory: the README and explain root say so, and status lists the servers Gwen's connection sees, so a link the operator adds is visible from Gwen's side
status names every server visible on Gwen's connection, and the docs state that a new link is a new reader of her memory

An ask is a background task, not a wait: the conversation stays usable while it runs, the page lists open background tasks with their age, the answer lands whenever it arrives (minutes or more), and an ask's expiry window is long enough for that, set by the operator per ask kind rather than by a turn clock (c38's derived window is the outer bound, never a turn deadline)
an answer arriving well after its turn ended, and after other turns in the same conversation, reaches that conversation and is marked late, by test

acceptance_criteria: embodiment/personas.py defines Persona (id, name, language he/en/none, length brief/conversational/detailed/unset, allow_formatting, translate_via role-name-or-None, mesh_enabled, text, default_role) and a built-in read-only Gwen persona; tests/test_personas.py passes

PersonaStore keeps personas.json 0600 under the state dir with a schema_version field; create/update/delete/list survive a reload; the built-in persona cannot be edited or deleted; a corrupt file degrades to built-in only with a recorded reason, never raises
translate_via is read only from the persona; no function in the module takes or inspects a model id string (AST or grep test)
tasks.instruction: Pure data + file IO, no daemon imports. Mirror daemon/reading.py for the 0600 atomic-write pattern. Language None means no language line at all. Persona text is operator-authored and capped in size (a named constant with its reason).

tasks.summary: Capabilities poller: the chat roles lobes serves (embodiment/capabilities.py)
acceptance_criteria: CapabilitiesPoller.snapshot() returns every /capabilities role whose path is /v1/chat/completions, each with role, model, ready, host (member/hosted_by or local) and the snapshot's age; tests/test_capabilities.py passes against a fake gateway

the poll interval is a named constant (60 s) with its reason; a role that turns not-ready shows not-ready in the next snapshot; a failed poll keeps the last snapshot, marks it stale and records a degradation, never raises
no code derives a role, capability or language from a model id (test)
tasks.instruction: Network only, keyed like realtime/client.py's _fetch_capabilities but reading every chat role. Role names come from the response keys; never parse model names.

tasks.summary: Per-role voice latency store and probe (embodiment/voice_latency.py)
acceptance_criteria: VoiceLatency keeps per-role and per-translator-combination samples 0600 under the state dir; state is unmeasured, probing or measured; p90 and a derived spoken deadline come from the samples; tests/test_voice_latency.py passes

probe(role, complete) runs a fixed small set of short spoken-style completions through an injected complete callable and records first-token or completion latency; live spoken turns can add samples; the derived deadline formula is a named function with its reason (lesson 1), never senses' 60 s by default
tasks.instruction: Injected callables only; no gateway client here. Follow daemon/app.py:derive_recall_deadline for how a derived clock is written and documented.

tasks.summary: Gwen's own mesh client, stdlib IRC to agentirc (embodiment/mesh_client.py)
acceptance_criteria: MeshClient connects as spark-gwen (nick from config, never from a model name), joins configured channels, sends PRIVMSG and delivers inbound PRIVMSG and mentions to a callback; tests/test_mesh_client.py passes against a fake asyncio IRC server
on ERR_NICKNAMEINUSE it records mesh-nick-taken, sends nothing and stays off; a dropped connection records a degradation and reconnects within a bounded, derived backoff; close(deadline) never raises
it reports the servers visible on its connection (for status and c53) and adds no dependency (tests/test_zero_deps.py unchanged)
tasks.instruction: asyncio streams only. Read agentirc/client.py (nick prefix rule, 433) and agentirc/protocol.py for the wire. No culture CLI subprocess. One connection per daemon; the daemon is the only sender as spark-gwen.

acceptance_criteria: AskBook keeps open asks 0600 under the state dir with ask id, conversation id, channel, posted time and expiry; an answer is attached to its ask and conversation after a daemon restart; past its window an ask becomes expired, shown, never dropped; tests/test_mesh_asks.py passes

bounds: at most one ask per turn; a turn started by any mesh message can reply but cannot ask; a cap on open asks; a rate cap on mesh-started turns; each tripped bound returns a recorded refusal; a scripted peer answering every ask with a question yields at most one post per operator turn
the default expiry window is hours (a named constant with its reason), so a two-hour-late answer still lands, marked late
tasks.instruction: Pure state + file IO. Answer matching is the documented rule in this module's docstring (see plan risk on matching); keep it one function so it can change.

tasks.summary: Translation hop around a chosen model (embodiment/translate.py)
acceptance_criteria: translated_complete(chosen, senses) wraps two complete callables: operator text is translated to English for the chosen role and its reply translated back to the persona language; the result carries both roles and both latencies; tests/test_translate.py passes

the operator's original text travels alongside the translation, so tool executors can use it: a remember call made in a translated turn receives the operator's own words and a search receives the operator's query (test with stub executors)
fenced data (recalled memory, library text, mesh text) is translated as quoted data, never promoted to instructions (test)
tasks.instruction: No edits to loop.py (it is byte-pinned). This is a seam wrapper the daemon applies when the persona's translate_via is set.

tasks.summary: CLI: spark-gwen identity in doctor and a mesh verb that prints, never runs (cli/_commands/mesh.py)
acceptance_criteria: embodiment mesh prints the nick, the channels, the env names and the culture registration steps (text and --json) and runs nothing (test that no subprocess is spawned); explain/catalog.py has the entry; tests/test_cli_introspection.py and the teken rubric pass
embodiment doctor reports spark-embodiment and spark-gwen as two identities that share no nick, socket or culture.yaml entry
tasks.instruction: Model it on cli/_commands/tunnel.py. Register in _build_parser().

tasks.summary: Culture-side ask: scratch probe, then draft the external-resident issue (no post)
acceptance_criteria: a scratch probe (outside the repo) shows whether a stdlib client with a spark-prefixed nick can join a channel on a test agentirc with no culture registration; the result is recorded on the frame

an issue draft for agentculture/culture asks for external-resident listing (manifest and residents view, no harness), sized by the probe; it is shown to the operator and posted only on the operator's go-ahead, via the communicate skill
tasks.instruction: Never run culture agents register or edit ~/.culture/server.yaml. The probe uses a throwaway agentirc instance on its own port.

tasks.summary: Persona-aware prompt parts: voice/typed split and tool-prompt language (embodiment/persona_prompt.py)
acceptance_criteria: compose_base(persona, path) returns exactly turn.SYSTEM_PROMPT for the built-in persona on the voice path, byte for byte; for the typed path it omits the voice-only speakability lines; tests/test_persona_prompt.py passes
for a non-default persona no fixed brevity line appears; the persona's length and language lines and its text appear in a fixed order; language None adds no language line
English renderings of the four tool prompts exist with the same obligation sentences; tool_prompt_language(persona) picks Hebrew for the built-in persona so its tool prompts stay byte-identical
tasks.instruction: Pure text. Do not edit turn.py's SYSTEM_PROMPT constant; split by composition. The obligation sentences (remember/forget/library/todos) are fixed; only their language and REMEMBER's length clause follow the persona.

tasks.summary: The ask_culture tool and its prompt line (embodiment/mesh_tools.py)
acceptance_criteria: build_mesh_tools returns an ask_culture ToolSpec whose executor posts only its question argument to an allow-listed channel and returns at once with an ask id; a non-listed channel, the switch off, or a tripped bound is a recorded refusal; tests/test_mesh_tools.py passes
a test plants recalled memory, library text and transcript text in the turn and asserts none of it reaches the post
mesh text returned to a turn is fenced and attributed like render_recalled output, and arms the write guard so remember, forget and set_todo_done refuse without the operator's own words (test)
tasks.instruction: Follow library/tools.py for fencing and daemon/todos.py for the guard. The prompt line steering the model is short and fixed, Hebrew and English renderings.

tasks.summary: Daemon wiring A: personas in the prompt, per-conversation persona, restore
acceptance_criteria: with the built-in persona the composed prompt passed to the seam for a spoken and for a typed turn is byte-identical to before (tests/test_turn.py:986-1002 and tests/test_daemon_app.py:2664 unmodified and green, plus a new byte test on the real composed prompt)

each conversation has a persona id recorded in every assistant transcript record; continuing a conversation restores it; a deleted persona on continue is a visible state that answers nothing; a turn snapshots the persona at its start
the tool registry, write guard and identity framing are identical with and without a persona; spoken replies still hit the 4000-character cap as a recorded truncation; loop.py is unchanged
tasks.instruction: Touch daemon/app.py (_compose_prompt, _complete_turn, _enter_conversation/_resumed_session) and session.py metadata only. New tests in tests/test_daemon_personas.py.

tasks.summary: Daemon wiring B: per-conversation model, distinct unavailable error, trace, voice gate
acceptance_criteria: seam() and the voice path read the conversation's role from one holder; summarise and recall-side calls stay on senses (test that a session summary names senses with worker chosen)

a 404 role_infeasible, 503 role_unverified or 429 from the chosen role yields a text-model-unavailable code distinct from the gateway-down code, and the fake gateway sees no second request (test over each status)
every assistant transcript record names role, model and host as the capabilities snapshot reported them; stt, tts, realtime and embedder requests are unchanged by the chosen role (test)
a spoken turn on an unmeasured role makes no completion request to it and shows probing or unavailable; after a recorded probe it uses the role with the derived deadline (test)
tasks.instruction: Touch daemon/app.py (http_complete, seam closure, summarise, _voice_complete, _text_complete). Choosing an unmeasured role triggers voice_latency.probe in the background. New tests in tests/test_daemon_models.py.

tasks.summary: Daemon wiring C: translator and the operator's words as the record
acceptance_criteria: with a persona's translate_via set, a typed and a spoken turn go through translate.translated_complete; the chosen role receives English and the operator receives the persona's language; the trace names both roles (test)
in a translated turn remember stores the operator's own words and search_library and search_conversations receive the operator's query; ContextPacket.original is the operator's text (test)
tasks.instruction: Touch daemon/app.py tool executor wiring only. New tests in tests/test_daemon_translate.py.

tasks.summary: HTTP routes: personas, models, conversation settings, status fields (http/server.py)
acceptance_criteria: guarded GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/personas, GET /api/models (the snapshot with voice-latency state), and optional persona, model and language fields on /api/chat, /api/clip and /api/conversation/new; tests/test_http_personas.py passes; every route is refused without the secret or a valid Access assertion
/api/status adds the capabilities snapshot age and roles, each live conversation's persona and role, and voice-latency states
tasks.instruction: Follow _todo_set_route and _read_route. ServerConfig gains callables; daemon/app.py passes them. No gateway key or secret in any payload.

tasks.summary: Daemon wiring D: mesh resident, inbound agent turns, asks, events, counters
acceptance_criteria: with EMBODIMENT_MESH on (default) the daemon starts MeshClient, binds ask_culture on every turn, and an agent mention starts a normal Gwen turn in a conversation labelled with the agent's nick; the reply is visible on the page before or as it is sent (test with a fake IRC server)

a mesh event kind (ask posted, answer arrived, ask expired, agent contacted, Gwen replied) is in tests/fixtures/events/schema.json, bus.py and web/src/api/events.ts; with live voice on and the floor free one spoken notice per agent conversation goes through Unprompted
status shows mesh state, nick, visible servers and asks posted/answered/expired counters that move on a scripted run; the mesh switch off refuses ask_culture and sends nothing
tasks.instruction: Touch daemon/app.py, bus.py, the events schema and web/src/api/events.ts only. The answer arrives through daemon/recall_events.py's Unprompted entry with its own dedup key.

tasks.summary: Web UI part 1: the settings row under the dock and the Personas tab (mockup v2)
acceptance_criteria: the dock-meta row shows Persona, Language (Hebrew, English, None) and Model menus opening upward, matching mockup v2's layout and interactions; the model menu greys not-ready roles and shows measured voice speed; Vitest tests for the menus pass
the Personas tab lists personas (built-in read-only), edits every persona field, shows the composed-prompt preview with persona and fixed sections, and saves through /api/personas
the unavailable banner reuses chat__degraded with its own text, the Model control turns amber, and one tap switches model; npm run build and the web lint pass
tasks.instruction: Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/PEUzLDEqvbEEc7DWN3LpuG (version 1793432718-7d11, approved; dimensions may be tuned). Use app.css/library.css tokens; dir=auto on every text node, labels outside it. Files: web/src/components/*, web/src/api/personas.ts, models.ts, App.tsx.

tasks.summary: Web UI part 2: mesh cards, agent conversations, open-asks count
acceptance_criteria: the ask card (waiting, answered, expired, late), the answer card (quoted, marked as another agent's words) and the agent-contacted card render from mesh events as in mockup v2; agent conversations appear in the Conversations list with the nick; the row shows the open-asks count; Vitest tests pass
tasks.instruction: Touch web/src components for the thread and HistoryPane; no new design beyond mockup v2.

tasks.summary: Docs and pinned tests: README, explain root, CLAUDE.md
acceptance_criteria: README and the explain root describe personas, model choice, the translator and spark-gwen, state that English is text-only while lobes has no English voice, and that a newly linked server can read Gwen's memory; tests/test_release_docs.py NOT_YET and TOOLS_BOUND are updated with ask_culture and pass

CLAUDE.md's cross-repo posting rule says Gwen's own mesh posts are hers by the operator's decision (q1) while issue posts stay the operator's; its role table is refreshed from a fresh /capabilities probe; the before-state quotes code at the export commit; markdownlint passes
tasks.instruction: Docs only, plus tests/test_release_docs.py. Re-probe /capabilities through grant run.

tasks.summary: Live acceptance on the rig, published as measured
acceptance_criteria: the after-state is walked once on the rig through the page: a persona created, one conversation per chat-ready role, a translated conversation, voice on a measured role, one mesh ask answered end to end and one agent-initiated conversation; each recorded with counters that moved

measured and published under docs/live-test-results/ with n stated: English remember/forget call rate (the d7 re-run), voice latency per role and with the translator, mesh answer latency; no claim that answers got better; bad numbers published as measured
tasks.instruction: Run under grant run on a test daemon (own port and state dir), never the public gwen-live unit. Operator listens and speaks for the voice parts.

risks.text: How an answer on the mesh is matched to its ask: agentirc has native threads (THREAD CREATE/REPLY, agentirc/skills/threads.py:165-292) and tags delivered messages with agentirc.io/thread and msgid (protocol.py:326-328) for clients that negotiate message-tags; each ask is posted as its own thread and matched by thread name first, then msgid, then the fallback rule (addressed to the nick in the ask's channel, most recent open ask, ambiguity shown). Residual: an agent that answers in the channel instead of the thread still hits the fallback
h45 was written for the marked policy ('a spoken turn's request names worker'); under the gated c51 it holds only once worker is measured, and t12 tests it in that state alongside h49
daemon/app.py is touched by t11, t12, t13, t14 and t15, so those waves are serial by construction; parallelism lives in wave 0

The English re-run of the remember/forget measurement (c36, d7 was 5 of 5 in Hebrew) may come back worse; if it does, English personas ship with that number published and the tool line is revised in a follow-up, not hidden

This branch stacks on feat/gwen-queries-the-library (0.23.0, embodiment#107, its live acceptance t9 not yet done); the work must rebase or merge onto main once #107 lands, per the squash-merged-stacked-PRs practice
The culture-side registration (t8's issue) may not land before this ships; Gwen still connects (agentirc accepts any spark- prefixed nick) but is not listed as a resident until culture supports it

t4's mesh client stays off on any 433, including the case where Gwen reconnects before the server has dropped her previous connection (her own ghost holds the nick); t15 should retry registration once after the server's ping timeout on a reconnect-time 433 and record mesh-nick-taken only if it persists

AskBook has no cancel: when the post fails after an ask is opened (ask-refused-post-failed), the ask stays open until it expires and holds one of the 8 open-ask slots; t15 should close it as failed (a small AskBook addition) rather than let failed posts exhaust the cap
